setupSteps: Pick the version. *Seated on a chair or bench (recommended first):* a firm chair with an upright back (no wheels, no arms that block the elbows) or a bench with back support. Sit all the way back, feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. *Standing:* feet hip-width, knees soft, weight even on the whole foot. *No equipment:* bottles or a rucksack in the same positions; or the pike push-up.

Overhead clearance check. Hold your arms straight up and check: nothing within an arm and a dumbbell's reach above (light fitting, ceiling fan, shelf, door frame); fan switched off and stopped; if it is too low, use a shortened lockout or the pike push-up.
Floor. A non-slip mat on a flat spot; chair on the mat or against a wall; a folded towel beside the chair to set the weights on.

Pick up the dumbbells safely. With the dumbbells on the floor, bend knees and hips and keep the back flat to lift them to the thighs, then kick or lift one at a time to shoulder height. Do not swing them up with the back.

Starting position. Dumbbells at shoulder height, forearms vertical, elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees (est.) and a little in front of the body, not straight out to the sides (sources say about 30 degrees in front of the line of the shoulders, the "scapular plane"; this is a coaching convention, one source says there is no single correct angle, so adjust to comfort; snippets).

Grip. *Neutral grip (recommended first):* palms facing each other, fingers toward the face; the easier-on-joints option most guides give. *Palms-forward:* knuckles pointing up, palms facing away; a common variant, but it asks more of the shoulder, so use a lighter weight. Wrists straight and stacked over the elbows. Grip firm, thumbs wrapped around the handle.

Brace. Ribs down toward the hips, glutes lightly squeezed (also in the seated version, feet pressing into the floor), tummy tight as if for a light punch, take a breath in before the first press (sources: brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes so the lower back does not arch; snippets).
Neck. Chin slightly tucked, eyes straight ahead, head back in line with the spine (do not push the head forward as the dumbbells rise).
Choose the weight. The lightest weight that lets you do 10 clean, slow reps with 3-4 left in the tank (section 7).

Camera. Phone in landscape at about chest height (110-130 cm, est.), 2-2.5 m away. Front view first for lockout and symmetry, side view next for back arch. Full body and the dumbbells above the head in frame.

Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, shoulder rolls and arm circles, cat-cow (Yoga & Stretch 10), thoracic rotation (Yoga & Stretch 7), and one set of 6-8 reps with very light dumbbells or empty hands.

steps.title: Sit tall with the dumbbells on the thighs
steps.action: Sit all the way back with feet flat, the dumbbells resting on the thighs.
steps.feel: A stable seat; weight through the sitting bones and feet.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back against the chair, head over shoulders. Front: shoulders level.

steps.title: Bring the dumbbells to shoulder height
steps.action: One at a time, lift each dumbbell to shoulder height (kick up with the knee if heavy), palms facing each other, elbows bent about 90 degrees and slightly in front.
steps.feel: Weight held by the arms, the shoulders not shrugged.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you lift each one.
steps.visualCheck: Front: wrists above elbows, forearms vertical, dumbbells beside the shoulders. Side: elbows slightly in front of the body.

steps.title: Brace
steps.action: Pull the ribs down, squeeze the glutes, tighten the tummy, tuck the chin slightly.
steps.feel: A tight, tall trunk; lower back long, not hollowed.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and hold a short breath of air for the brace, then let it out on the press (do not hold it throughout).
steps.visualCheck: Side: ribs and hips stacked, no gap between lower back and chair back (seated) or a straight line from ear to hip to ankle (standing).

steps.title: Press the dumbbells up
steps.action: Press both dumbbells up and slightly together in an arc until the arms are almost straight, with the hands above the shoulders.
steps.feel: The shoulders and back of the arms working; the shoulders not shrugged into the ears.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both arms rise together and finish at the same height; side: dumbbells travel up over the shoulders, not out in front; the back stays against the chair or stays straight.

steps.title: Finish with a soft lockout
steps.action: Reach the top with the arms nearly straight (a very slight bend; one source warns to stop before hard lockout, snippet), dumbbells over the shoulders, ribs still down.
steps.feel: Weight stacked over the shoulders; no pinching in the shoulder.
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbow angle at or above about 165 degrees (est.), arms level with each other. Side: ears, shoulders and hips stacked, no arched back.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbells slowly back to shoulder height (one source cues pulling them down with the back muscles rather than letting them drop; snippet).
steps.feel: A controlled stretch of the shoulders and the back of the arms.
steps.visualCheck: Front: forearms vertical again, elbows slightly in front; side: the same path back down; no hip shift or back lean.

steps.title: Reset and repeat
steps.action: At the bottom, check the wrists, ribs and glutes, take a breath in, and press again.
steps.breathing: Normal; breathe out on each press.
steps.visualCheck: Both arms follow the same path and range.

steps.title: Set the dumbbells down safely
steps.action: After the last rep, lower the dumbbells to the thighs, then to the floor on a towel or mat with a 2-3 s count and a flat back; do not drop them from shoulder height.
steps.feel: Controlled arms and legs, no back rounding.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat while lowering; the only sound is a soft touch.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Arching the lower back. Why: puts load on the lower spine; one source calls excessive lower-back extension the number-one cause of lower-back pain from overhead presses (snippet). Fix: ribs down, glutes tight, lighter weight, seated with back support.

commonMistakes.title: Weight too heavy
commonMistakes.text: Weight too heavy. Why: forces compensation in the neck and back (snippet) and a short range. Fix: choose the weight by 3-4 reps in reserve (section 7).

commonMistakes.title: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
commonMistakes.text: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides. Why: can stress the shoulder joint; ACE material says the shoulder blade plane (about 30-35 degrees forward of the sides, snippet) gives the joint room and frontal-plane pressing with the arm rotated outward can cause impingement (snippet). Fix: elbows slightly in front, wrists over elbows.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears. Why: the upper trapezius and neck take over. Fix: shoulders down at the start; press the weights up, not the shoulders.

commonMistakes.title: Pushing the head forward or looking up
commonMistakes.text: Pushing the head forward or looking up. Why: strains the neck. Fix: chin tucked, head stays stacked over the shoulders as the weights pass.

commonMistakes.title: Pressing out in front instead of overhead
commonMistakes.text: Pressing out in front instead of overhead. Why: turns it into a front raise, loads the shoulder joint badly. Fix: dumbbells finish over the shoulders; check the side view.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the dumbbells fast or bouncing at the bottom (momentum)
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the dumbbells fast or bouncing at the bottom (momentum). Why: jerks the shoulder and elbow. Fix: 3 s lowering and a calm start for each rep.

commonMistakes.title: Hard-locking the elbows or stopping short
commonMistakes.text: Hard-locking the elbows or stopping short. Why: hard lockout jams the elbow (MasterClass, snippet); a short press cuts the work. Fix: nearly straight with a soft bend, and the same range each rep.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (breathing study PubMed 7741618, carried from earlier items). Fix: breathe out on the press, in on the lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the weights at the end or hitting the floor
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the weights at the end or hitting the floor. Why: noise for neighbours below and risk to feet and the chair. Fix: lower to the thighs, then to a mat with a 2-3 s count; keep feet clear.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring the ceiling and the fan
commonMistakes.text: Ignoring the ceiling and the fan. Why: injury and damage. Fix: do the clearance check (section 3) every time.

safetyNotes: Shoulder problems and impingement: the shoulder-pain sources suggest that overhead pressing is often the hardest movement when the shoulder hurts, the pain tends to come in the middle of the arm lift (a painful arc), and that people often modify with a more horizontal press, a smaller range, a narrower or different grip, lighter weight or less weekly volume (physio and clinic blogs, snippets; practice-based, not controlled trials). Stop if the shoulder pinches or the pain sharpens; ask a clinician. Clinical guidance for the dumbbell press itself: Not found.

Lower back problems: the seated press with back support is the usual starting point (snippets), keep the ribs down, no arching, stop if pain increases or spreads down a leg. Clinical guidance specific to this lift: Not found.
Neck pain: pushing the head forward or shrugging can irritate the neck; lower the weight and keep the chin tucked.

High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the press, do not hold the breath, use light weight and moderate effort; overhead arm work raises the heart's workload for the same weight in some people, so get medical clearance first with heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure (clinical source for the overhead position specifically: Not found).

Osteoporosis: loaded strength work is generally recommended; the LIFTMOR trial used supervised overhead presses in postmenopausal women with low bone density (snippet) but it is not a template for unsupervised home use; avoid arching and loaded twisting; with a vertebral fracture, severe osteoporosis or kyphosis, ask a clinician first (snippets).

Pregnancy and postpartum: resistance training is generally supported in uncomplicated pregnancy (PMC review, snippet); sources differ on overhead presses: one lists overhead lifting after the first trimester as something to avoid (Healthline), another lists a light overhead press as acceptable with a stop rule for dizziness and headache (perinatology.com), and pregnancy trainers suggest a seated or supported press with ribs down and a landmine or incline press as alternatives (snippets); ACOG's own wording was not reached (Committee Opinion 804 was named but not read), so ask your obstetrician, midwife or women's health physiotherapist; stop with dizziness, headache, pelvic heaviness, leaking or pain.

Mumbai flat: put the chair on a non-slip mat or against a wall; check the ceiling height and switch off and stop the fan before pressing; set the dumbbells down gently on a mat or towel; do not drop them on a tile floor; no glass bottles; keep clear of the balcony slab and open windows; do not press near a door frame.
